key_insight: Atomic MathReasoner improves mathematical LLMs by selecting a problem-specific composition of specialized reasoning skills rather than treating reasoning as one monolithic capability.
engineering_relevance: A lightweight router selects among precomputed LoRA expert compositions, enabling adaptive specialization without costly online optimization.
method: Train capability-specific LoRA experts and discover low-loss composition prototypes through gradient-free optimization on held-out validation subsets.
Score prototypes using reference-solution token-level negative log-likelihood and filter ambiguous assignments with a confidence margin.
Distill the resulting pseudo-labels into a router that selects a composition prototype for each input problem.
evidence_signal: On AtomicMath with Qwen2.5-Math-Instruct-7B, AMR raises average field accuracy from 64.4% to 68.1% at Level 1 and 59.3% to 63.7% at Level 2, and average logical reasoning performance from 39.4% to 46.8%.
watch_item: Generalization beyond AtomicMath remains unestablished in the abstract, and deployment requires offline expert training, prototype optimization, and router supervision.
paper_title: Atomic MathReasoner: Instance-Level Composition of Atomic Reasoning Skills for Mathematical LLMs
